The fix is one line: the fraction is trimmed of trailing zeros, then padded to at least two digits (`1.5` → `1.50`, `2` → `2.00`, `1.25` stays `1.25`, `1.123` stays `1.123`). Trimming only removes zeros that `parseNear` pads back in, so no digits are lost.

`bun test` passes 3 of 3. I also checked the edge cases by reasoning, since my attempt to run an ad-hoc script was blocked: `0` gives `0.00`, 1 yoctoNEAR keeps all 24 digits, and `10^30` gives `1000000.00`. I did not execute those cases.
